title: The AIR Sound
kidRule: The 'air' sound has three main spellings: A-I-R like in REPAIR, A-R-E like in CAREFUL, and sometimes E-A-R like in UNDERWEAR. E-A-R is the tricky one, because it usually says 'ear' like in HEAR!
hint: Listen for the 'air' sound. It has a few different spellings. Picture the word in your mind: which one looks right?
reminder: The 'air' sound has a few spellings: A-I-R, A-R-E, and E-A-R. If one did not work, try another one!

check.question: Why is REPAIR spelled with A-I-R?
check.correctAnswer: Because A-I-R is one of the ways to spell the 'air' sound!
distractors: Because the letter I is always silent
Because every word that ends in R needs two vowels

words.def: Paying attention so that nothing goes wrong.
words.sent: Be careful when you carry the hot soup.
words.story: A mother crocodile is very careful. She carries her tiny babies to the water inside her huge mouth without hurting them!
words.card: Be *careful*, a cow is driving that *car*!

words.def: To fix something that is broken.
words.sent: Dad will repair the wheel on my bike.
words.story: A sea star can repair itself! If it loses an arm, it slowly grows a new one.
words.card: I need a *pair* of robots to *repair* my wobbly sandcastle!

words.def: A place where milk is kept and made into foods like cheese and butter.
words.sent: The dairy sells fresh milk and cheese.
words.story: Milk, cheese, butter, and yogurt are all dairy foods. It takes about ten pounds of milk to make one pound of cheese!
words.card: The cow jumped in the *air* when the *dairy* ran out of ice cream!

words.def: To watch out for something that could cause trouble.
words.sent: The sign said to beware of the grumpy goose.
words.story: In the ancient city of Pompeii, a floor picture made of tiny tiles shows a dog with words that mean 'Beware of the dog'. It is about 2,000 years old!
words.card: *Beware*! There *are* jellybeans hiding in your slippers!

words.def: The clothes you put on first, next to your skin, beneath your other clothes.
words.sent: He packed socks and clean underwear for the trip.
words.story: There is no washing machine on the International Space Station, so astronauts wear their clothes for days and then throw them away!
words.card: The superhero hid *under* the bed because his *underwear* had ducks on it!

words.def: A huge, flat stretch of grassy land with very few trees.
words.sent: Bison once roamed across the wide prairie.
words.story: Prairie dogs are not dogs at all. They are chubby ground squirrels that live in underground towns!
words.card: The *prairie* wind tossed my hat high in the *air*, and a bison caught it!

words.def: To get ready, or to get something ready.
words.sent: We prepare a picnic every Sunday.
words.story: Squirrels prepare for winter by burying thousands of nuts. They forget some, and those can grow into new trees!
words.card: We *are* going to *prepare* spaghetti for a hundred hungry penguins!

words.def: To say something in a loud, clear, and sure way.
words.sent: I declare this the best sandcastle ever built!
words.story: In 1776, American leaders signed a famous paper to declare that their country was free. One of them, John Hancock, signed his name extra big!
words.card: I *declare* that we *are* having pancakes for dinner!

words.def: So unpleasant or painful that it is very hard to put up with.
words.sent: The smell of the old socks was unbearable.
words.story: Desert heat can feel unbearable. Death Valley in California holds the record for the hottest air ever measured on Earth: 134 degrees Fahrenheit!
words.card: The *bear* said the smell of my socks was *unbearable*!

words.def: A person who has at least one million dollars.
words.sent: The millionaire gave money to build a new library.
words.story: A stack of one million one-dollar bills would be about 358 feet tall. That is taller than the Statue of Liberty!
words.card: The *lion* became a *millionaire* by selling roaring lessons!
